study.title: Steroids Helping Albuterol Responders Exclusively
study.summary: The purpose of the study is to determine whether corticosteroids are beneficial to children with bronchiolitis whose breathing gets better after being given a breathing treatment with albuterol.
study.inclusion_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* diagnosis of bronchiolitis
* Respiratory Distress Assessment Index score of 4 or more
study.exclusion_criteria:
* prior prescription of bronchodilators or inhaled corticosteroids
* birth at \<36 weeks gestation
* chronic cardiac disease
* chronic pulmonary disease (including asthma)
* immunodeficiency
* non-topical steroid use in the prior week
* parents that don't understand English
* baseline systolic blood pressure \>118 mmHg
* home oxygen use
* evidence of systemic fungal or varicella infection
* bronchodilator use in the prior week
* allergy to albuterol or corticosteroids

interventions.name: prednisolone or methylprednisolone
interventions.description: either prednisolone 2mg/kg PO once daily or methylprednisolone 1.6mg/kg IV once daily (if IV access is present) for length of hospitalization, for a maximum of seven days

primary_outcomes.measure: respiratory rate and respiratory distress score
length of hospitalization (actual and until meets "ready for discharge" criteria)
primary_outcomes.time_frame: variable, likely no more than 2 weeks

secondary_outcomes.measure: need for increased respiratory support (intubation, CPAP, BiPAP)
amount of oxygen used during hospitalization
number of doses of bronchodilators used during hospitalization
secondary_outcomes.time_frame: variable, likely no more than 2 weeks
variable, likely no more than 3 weeks

secondary_outcomes.measure: need for unanticipated medical care after discharge
secondary_outcomes.time_frame: variable, likely no more than 3 weeks
variable, likely no more than 2 weeks

study.why_stopped: We were unable to enroll a sufficient number of patients due to manpower.
